concerns.text: The completed-work list claims `code/correlate_bulk.py` satisfies FR-009–FR-011, but the plan (Phase 3) explicitly EXCLUDES correlation (c) 'interaction-energy error vs viscosity' required by FR-009, substituting 'dispersion-only error vs viscosity'. No task restores FR-009(c) coverage and no spec amendment authorizes the narrowing — a silent requirement weakening baked into 'completed' history.

concerns.location: tasks.md:Completed work (fallback dataset) vs constitution.md:Principle VI
concerns.text: Tasks preserve as verified a benchmark against a 'curated synthetic test set' (20 pairs, seed 42) rather than real CCSD(T)/CBS reference energies. Constitution Principle VI requires benchmarking against high-level ab initio reference energies for the same ion pairs; the spec was never amended to authorize synthetic references, so the completed work — and T067's re-validation of it — enshrines a constitution violation.

T067 validates contracts against `specs/001-transferability-of-dft-d3-dispersion-to-/contracts/`, but the plan's project structure places the spec under `specs/PROJ-735-transferability-of-dft-d3-dispersion-to-/`. The path mismatch makes the verification step check the wrong (or nonexistent) directory.

concerns.location: tasks.md:T065/T067 vs spec.md:FR-007 + US-2 Scenario 2 + contracts/scaling_factor.schema.yaml
concerns.text: US-2 demands a p<0.05 significance test, FR-007 defines rejection via bootstrap-CI exclusion of 1.0, and the scaling_factor contract requires a `p_value` field. No task reconciles which test is actually produced; T065's calibration section will cite numbers whose provenance/test definition remains contradictory.

Tasks treat the 20-pair set as final ('the study remains the specified 20-pair benchmark') while the spec still assumes ≥100 pairs (≤500 cap). The deviation is documented in reports but the spec assumption is never amended, leaving the tasks in numeric contradiction with the spec they claim to satisfy.

T065 addresses the calibration question but no task records a decision (accept/defer/push back) on the reviewer's requested experimentally measured lattice-energy benchmark, leaving that objection unaddressed in any artifact.
